title: Leakage-Safe Covariate Handling in CPM
text: covariates regressed full dataset cross-validation, held-test information leaks training pipeline. can inflate distort --sample performance. cpmr, leakage-safe behavior means: fit covariate regression fold’s training split ; apply learned regression parameters train test data inside fold; keep parameter-learning steps (example scaling model selection) inside CV well.

title: Leakage-Safe Covariate Handling in CPM
code: set.seed(123) n <- 80 p <- 120  # Synthetic connectivity matrix (rows = subjects, cols = edges) conmat <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p)  # A synthetic covariate (for example age-like nuisance variable) covariates <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1)  # Build behavior with both signal and covariate effects edge_signal <- rowMeans(conmat[, 1:10, drop = FALSE]) behav <- 0.7 * edge_signal + 0.6 * covariates[, 1] + rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)  # Leakage-safe CPM call: covariates are handled fold-wise inside assessment res <- cpm(   conmat = conmat,   behav = behav,   spec = spec(),   covariates = covariates,   resamples = 5 )  summary(res) #> CPM summary: #>   Number of folds: 5 #>   Pooled correlations (Pearson): #>     Joint: 0.241 #>     Positive: 0.261 #>     Negative: -0.104 #>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson): #>     Joint: 0.265 (SE 0.136) (5/5 folds) #>     Positive: 0.291 (SE 0.134) (5/5 folds) #>     Negative: -0.270 (1/5 folds) #>   Pooled RMSE: #>     Joint: 0.518 #>     Positive: 0.513 #>     Negative: 0.529 #>   Pooled MAE: #>     Joint: 0.407 #>     Positive: 0.411 #>     Negative: 0.387 #>   Selected edges: #>     Positive: 1.67% #>     Negative: 0.17%

title: Native Getting Started with cpmr
text: CPM expects one row per subject one column per edge. conmat: n x p connectivity matrix; behav: length-n numeric outcome vector; covariates: optional n x q nuisance matrix.
code: library(cpmr)  withr::local_seed(123) n <- 80 p <- 200  conmat <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), nrow = n, ncol = p) covariates <- matrix(rnorm(n), ncol = 1) behav <- rowMeans(conmat[, 1:12, drop = FALSE]) +   0.5 * covariates[, 1] +   rnorm(n, sd = 0.5)

title: Native Getting Started with cpmr
text: Use cpm() spec() object --sample estimate predictive performance. keeps CPM-specific steps covariate handling, edge selection, model training inside assessment fold.
code: result <- cpm(   conmat = conmat,   behav = behav,   spec = spec(),   covariates = covariates,   resamples = 5 )  result #> CPM: #>   Call: cpm(conmat = conmat, behav = behav, spec = spec(), covariates = covariates,  #>     resamples = 5) #>   Number of folds: 5 #>   Number of observations: 80 #>     Complete cases: 80 #>   Parameters: #>     Covariates:            included #>     Missing data:          fail #>     Edge storage:          summed across folds #>     Selection:             pearson / p_value / 0.01 #>     Construction:          separate / no weighting / raw edges #>     Model:                 linear regression #>   Use summary() for aggregate metrics and tidy() for metric tables. summary(result) #> CPM summary: #>   Number of folds: 5 #>   Pooled correlations (Pearson): #>     Joint: -0.084 #>     Positive: 0.062 #>     Negative: -0.177 #>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson): #>     Joint: -0.071 (SE 0.045) (5/5 folds) #>     Positive: 0.030 (SE 0.055) (5/5 folds) #>     Negative: -0.174 (SE 0.097) (3/5 folds) #>   Pooled RMSE: #>     Joint: 0.705 #>     Positive: 0.644 #>     Negative: 0.701 #>   Pooled MAE: #>     Joint: 0.573 #>     Positive: 0.515 #>     Negative: 0.558 #>   Selected edges: #>     Positive: 1.00% #>     Negative: 0.50%

title: Native Getting Started with cpmr
text: CPM results keep observation-level predictions object, summary() reports pooled RMSE MAE, pooled --fold correlations, mean fold-wise correlations. Use tidy() obtain pooled metrics per-fold correlation table. three outputs slightly different jobs: summary(result) prints default aggregate report; summary(result)[["metrics"]] exposes compact summary-level metric table stored summary object; tidy(result, component = "metrics") returns raw fold-wise metric table filtering, plotting, export, level = "pooled" returns pooled metrics. default, cpm() uses 10-fold assessment return_edges = "sum". Ten folds require least 10 complete cases; around 30 cases rough minimum least 3 observations per assessment fold, guarantee stable correlations. Smaller assessment folds trigger warning, prioritize RMSE MAE, mark pooled --fold correlations descriptive. Explicit leave-one-assessment available resamples = NULL. default, cpm() stores fold-aggregated edge selection counts. makes edge summaries immediately available common fold-based workflow. want control edge storage explicitly: predictions returns one row per original observation. na_action = "exclude" removed subjects fitting, rows still present fold value NA. return_edges = "sum", cpmr stores fold-summed edge counts edge. memory matters, switch return_edges = "none" use return_edges = "" fold-wise edge arrays truly needed.

text: Shape connectivity matrix subjects--edges matrix, row contains edge vector one subject, pair behavioral vector. native workflow uses spec() together cpm(). spec() can also express richer CPM variants without leaving native API surface: keeps main CPM stages visible grouping naturally paired options small helpers: selection = cpm_selection_cor(...) defines edges screened; construction = cpm_construction_strength(...) defines screened edges become CPM-derived predictors; model = cpm_model_lm() defines outcome model fitted predictors. default, spec() keeps edge standardization turned native workflow stays close classic CPM path screening edges, constructing summary features, fitting outcome model. want fold-local edge z-scoring, opt cpm_construction_strength(standardize_edges = TRUE). new CPM, key idea behind current summary-based construction : positive edges edges whose screening association outcome positive passes threshold; negative edges edges whose screening association outcome negative passes threshold; CPM collapses screened edge sets subject-level summary features fitting outcome model. sign_mode = "separate", cpmr keeps positive negative summaries separate predictors reports three prediction streams: joint, fits one model summaries together; positive, positive-diagnostic stream; negative, negative-diagnostic stream. sign_mode = "net", cpmr constructs single net_summary = positive_summary - negative_summary feature returns one net prediction stream. cpm() fold-based: runs CPM requested assessment plan returns --fold predictions together fold structure. summary(result) reports pooled --fold RMSE MAE, pooled correlations, mean fold-wise correlations. pooled metrics available tables tidy(result, component = "metrics", level = "pooled"); fold-wise correlations returned level = "foldwise". cpm() defaults 10-fold assessment. requires least 10 complete cases; around 30 cases rough minimum least 3 observations assessment fold, guarantee stable correlations. title: Define CPM strength-construction settings — cpm_construction_strength
text: Build feature-construction portion spec(). helper configures current CPM path turns screened edges subject-level strength-style predictors. name uses "strength" stage follows CPM tradition constructing subject-level scores screened edge sets, limited simple raw network-strength sum: positive negative edges can represented separately collapsed net score, optional weighting can applied score formed, edge values can standardized within training set constructing final predictors.

title: Define CPM strength-construction settings — cpm_construction_strength
code: cpm_construction_strength(   sign_mode = c("separate", "net"),   weight_scale = 0,   standardize_edges = FALSE )

title: Define CPM strength-construction settings — cpm_construction_strength
text: sign_mode positive negative screened information represented. "separate" constructs positive_summary negative_summary, fits joint stream together, also returns positive negative positive-/ negative-diagnostic streams. "net" constructs one net_summary = positive_summary - negative_summary feature returns single net stream. weight_scale Non-negative scale controlling optional sigmoid-style edge weighting strength construction. 0 disables additional weighting keeps classic hard-threshold CPM score. Values greater 0 apply current sigmoid weighting scheme, larger values producing smoother transition around selection cutoff. standardize_edges Logical value indicating edge values standardized within training set CPM feature construction. TRUE, edge centered scaled unit variance using training data, transformation applied prediction time. follows fold-local edge z-scoring approach described Rapuano et al. (2020). Defaults FALSE default construction stays close classic CPM strength workflow; set TRUE want additional preprocessing step explicitly.

title: Define a CPM specification — spec
text: spec() keeps main CPM decisions visible top level grouping stage-specific settings helpers. spec() groups CPM settings three stages: cpm_selection_cor() configures current correlation-based edge selection path. cpm_construction_strength() configures current strength-construction path. cpm_model_lm() defines outcome model fitted CPM-derived features.

title: Define a CPM specification — spec
code: s <- spec(   selection = cpm_selection_cor(     method = "spearman",     criterion = "absolute",     level = 0.1   ),   construction = cpm_construction_strength(     sign_mode = "net",     weight_scale = 0.03   ),   model = cpm_model_lm() ) s #> CPM specification: #>   Selection: #>     Method:                spearman #>     Criterion:             absolute #>     Level:                 0.1 #>   Construction: #>     Sign mode:             net #>     Edge weighting:        sigmoid #>     Weight scale:          0.03 #>     Edge standardization:  none #>   Model: #>     Outcome model:         linear regression  conmat <- matrix(rnorm(100 * 100), nrow = 100) behav <- rnorm(100) result <- cpm(   conmat = conmat,   behav = behav,   spec = s,   resamples = 5 ) summary(result) #> CPM summary: #>   Number of folds: 5 #>   Pooled correlations (Pearson): #>     Net: 0.007 #>   Fold-wise correlations (Pearson): #>     Net: 0.020 (SE 0.094) (5/5 folds) #>   Pooled RMSE: #>     Net: 1.190 #>   Pooled MAE: #>     Net: 0.883 #>   Selected edges: #>     Positive: 22.40% #>     Negative: 15.60%

title: cpmr (development version)
text: cpm() now uses staged specification created spec(). old thresh_method, thresh_level, kfolds, bias_correct arguments replaced spec, resamples, staged helper constructors. Unused arguments passed ... now cause error rather ignored. Removed deprecated confounds alias. Use covariates instead. returned cpm object now stores workflow state spec, settings, predictions, folds. Code accessed old real, pred, params fields must updated.

title: cpmr (development version)
text: Added spec() together cpm_selection_cor(), cpm_construction_strength(), cpm_model_lm() make screening, summarization, outcome-model choices explicit. cpm() now defaults 10-fold assessment; explicit leave-one-manual assessment plans remain available resamples. summary.cpm() tidy.cpm() report pooled RMSE/MAE alongside correlation metrics. Small assessment folds trigger warning, make fold-wise correlations unavailable, identify pooled --fold correlations descriptive; fold-wise summaries report number contributing folds. Unweighted edge standardization now processes selected edges constructing training assessment features, reducing time memory use sparse edge selections. Fold execution discards intermediate model state fit instead retaining predictions assembled. Fold-wise edge storage avoids copying full edge array every fold. Reworked package documentation pkgdown navigation around spec() + cpm() workflow, including native getting-started vignette.

title: cpmr (development version)
text: Corrected covariate-adjusted p-value screening degrees freedom predictions rank-deficient nuisance regressions. Simplified internal CPM workflow around fold-based execution aligned tests/testthat current R/ modules. Hardened assessment-fold validation leakage-safe preprocessing fold must retain least 3 complete-case training observations.
